honesty.status: AUTHORED and DERIVED: every course is a grouping and an order chosen by the rules printed under `rules`; every name, title, room label and count is READ from the registry that owns it. Nothing is fetched and no model runs.
honesty.content: unverified general practice. The lessons a course lists have not been reviewed by a journey-level practitioner, and grouping them does not change that.
honesty.not_certification: no course certifies, qualifies or permits anybody to do anything. Finishing every lesson in a course leaves a learner with exactly the standing they started with.
honesty.not_a_gate: prerequisites are the ladder's advice about order. Nothing is locked, and the unaided verification gate that schools/ declares stays where it is.
honesty.bands: K-12 bands are DERIVED from the words of each band's offer in schools/; they are a reading of that offer, not a placement by any teacher or district. School districts named elsewhere remain PROPOSED partners.
honesty.seat_time: no minutes are given: no scenario declares a duration, so a course counts seat runs instead of inventing a time.

rules.trade_course: one per hall of pack/registry/halls.json: the lessons standing in that hall, grouped under the hall's district
rules.strand_course: one per room of web/interiors.py: every lesson whose strand it is, across halls
rules.order: ladder depth (lessons.json#ladder.depth), then the lessons registry order
rules.prerequisites: the ladder's own edges, split into those inside the course and those pointing at another course; advice about order, never a gate
rules.seat_time: counts only - seats bound to the course halls, seat runs, walkaround points and crew asks; no minutes, because no scenario declares a duration

K-5.rests_on: no machine seats and no station quizzes
K-5.why: awareness only: a K-5 lesson is one walked through rooms, read at the door and asked of an advisor - no seat, no walkaround of a seat, no crew, no station, no crib check

6-8.rests_on: home modules at fundamentals tier plus class station work
6-8.why: fundamentals tier and class-stage steps only: no simulator floor time is offered to this band

9-10.why: up to applied tier, class and floor steps

11-12.why: every tier, class and floor steps

bands.offer: awareness only: the campus maps, the walkable halls and the city layers; no machine seats and no station quizzes
home modules at fundamentals tier plus class station work
applied-tier modules, stations, and simulator floor time with the regional scenario
mastery-tier modules, full flipped loop, and the unaided verification gate

concepts.text: On old work the mortar is meant to be the sacrificial part, and the tool you choose decides whether it stays that way.
Issue, calibration and return all happen in one place, and the discipline is the lesson.
Work the bench and treat joint finish as an outcome of the tool rather than a decoration.

The joint is the part of the wall the weather reaches first, and its profile decides whether water runs off or stands. Tooling compacts the mortar as it shapes it, and much of what a concave joint does for weathering it does because it was pressed, not because of its shape alone.
Tooling is compaction; the profile is what is left behind afterwards.

Replacement is what you do when repair has been proved impossible, not when it looks slower.

concepts.text: A lining that is rushed to temperature destroys itself from the inside, invisibly, on the first day.
The practice floor is where the mock-up stands, which is the only place to learn this cheaply.
Read what the floor is held to before the mock-up is lit; heat changes what the room requires of you.
Work the bench and read the doctrine line as the thing you will be tempted to ignore.

A refractory lining spends its life travelling up and down through temperatures that move every joint in it. It is built to expand: joints are laid tight and the expansion is allowed for deliberately, and the dry-out afterwards drives the water out slowly enough that steam does not lift the work it is leaving.
A lining fails at the joint it was never allowed to move.

concepts.text: This hall teaches atmospheric testing, retrieval, patient packaging, and all of it is set out from marks somebody made, so the first question is how far those marks can be trusted.

A mark everything else is measured from, put in once and protected. Measure from the control point, never from the last thing you set - that is how a small error becomes a cumulative one, and it is the habit this floor exists to build.

supplement_rules.glossary: the rooms and off-room places the lesson stands in (meaning: web/interiors.py purpose, lessons.json off_room_places), every tool of the hall's district crib (meaning: the tool's own `use` line), every PPE item and hazard on the condition record of a room the lesson walks (meaning: where it is listed - the record gives no definition, so none is written), the seats, scenarios and walkaround points the lesson runs (meaning: task, brief, check), the advisors and crew roles it asks (meaning: role, job)
supplement_rules.concepts: the lesson's own `why`, every step note, then from the owning registry: a station's lesson and doctrine, an advisor or crew topic's `say` (or, for a `read` topic, the binding it is read from), a crew role's stop condition, a scenario's `teaches`, a walkaround point's check, and the crib drill contract
supplement_rules.safety: labelled unverified general practice. The condition record of every room the lesson walks, quoted in the exact form the 3D page's condLine() prints it (a placard hangs only where the record asks for PPE), the walkaround fault line and the crew stop-work lines of the steps that bind them, the checklist of a station step, and the lesson's limits
supplement_rules.questions: one per walk, placard, advisor, walkaround, sim, crew and station step, plus one crib drill item for every lesson (two when the lesson runs the crib check); each answer is a registry id with the pointer it resolves at, the distractors are siblings from the same record, and the correct option's position is index arithmetic
supplement_rules.worksheet: one line per step: the step's own `do` line, verbatim, and a fill-in prompt for its kind
supplement_rules.where: the rooms and places walked, the hall's district crib, the advisors asked (and the room each stands in), the seats and scenarios run, the crews asked, the stations taken, and links to the lesson, the hall in 3D and the ladder
